title: fix(ui): keep async question actions out of the live region
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #185716.

An async question card puts `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` on `.chat-question-summary`, and that container also holds the card's Retry and Answer buttons. Live regions should not contain focusable controls, so those controls become part of every announcement and focusing one interrupts it.

## User Impact

Async question cards now announce their text without repeating the action buttons. Both buttons render and work exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` sat on the `.chat-question-summary` wrapper, which also contains the Retry and Answer `<button>` elements. Focusable controls inside a live region are re-announced on every update, and focusing one interrupts the reader mid-sentence.

Wrap only the card text in the live region, leaving both buttons outside it. The visible markup is unchanged; the wrapper keeps `.chat-question-summary` and the assertions that read its `textContent` still hold.

## Evidence

Latest exact-head verification on `050c1fe71c7923461977f2153829b86c26bed5f4`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185565#issuecomment-6438236929. Two fresh built-Gateway Chromium runs confirm Retry restored inline beside the label, separate polite delivery/error text regions, controls outside live regions, 3px question gaps, and keyboard Retry preserving the payload. Includes an inspected fresh screenshot. Earlier layout-placement question is resolved by this head.

Independent built-Gateway Chromium comparison (main twice, original head twice, current head twice), CDP accessibility-tree ancestry, measured row gaps, keyboard controls, and inspected before/after screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185565#issuecomment-6437299418. The earlier `ea652126a14` head restored delivery/error live semantics and the 3px question-row gap, but moved Retry below the error. That intermediate layout regression is resolved by `050c1fe71c`; see the latest evidence above. This is accessibility-tree proof, not recorded screen-reader speech.

Rendered the card markup in Chromium before and after the change and read the live region directly.

| | Live region | Focusable descendants | Buttons rendered |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | `div.chat-question-summary` | `Retry`, `Answer` | 2 |
| After | inner text wrapper | none | 2 |

Visible text after the change is unchanged: `Which audience? In composer Queued Retry Answer`.

A static scan of the modified file reports no `<button>` inside the `aria-live` region; the same scan on the base revision reports two.

### Review feedback fixed on this head

ClawSweeper's review on `f433ab05e71` found two real defects in the first split.

**1. Delivery announcements were dropped (P2).** The first split moved only the question/answer
text into the region and left `deliveryLabel` and `sendError` outside it. A queued answer that
changed from sending to failed no longer announced "Answer not sent" or its error — a regression
against the delivery feedback PR #154486 explicitly preserved. Head `6789fc4f769` keeps the delivery
label and error inside a nested live region and leaves only the Retry button outside.

**2. Multi-question row gap collapsed (P3).** The unstyled wrapper made every question an ordinary
block child of one grid item, so multiple questions lost the 3px grid gap. The wrapper now keeps the
`display: grid; gap: 3px` the questions had directly on `.chat-question-summary`.

### Real-browser proof

`chat-async-question-live-region.browser.test.tsx` runs in the repo's Chromium browser project
against the shipped component with the real stylesheets, so both findings are measured rather than
inferred.

Red on `f433ab05e71`:

```
× keeps delivery status and error announced while Retry stays out of every live region
  AssertionError: expected 'Everyone' to contain 'Answer not sent'
× keeps the grid row gap between multiple questions
  AssertionError: expected 'block' to be 'grid'
```

The second message is the P3 finding proven directly: the previous wrapper computed to `display:
block`, so the questions stopped being grid items.

Green on this head: `2 passed (2)`. The test reads the computed layout — the announcement wrapper
is `display: grid` with `row-gap: 3px`, and the two question blocks have a non-zero measured gap
between their bounding rects.

### Regression, red on the previous head and green on this head

`chat-async-question-live-region.test.tsx` mounts the real `AsyncQuestionSummary`, drives a failed
queued answer, and asserts the delivery status and error sit inside an `[aria-live="polite"]` region
while the Retry button does not.

On `f433ab05e71` (2 failed):

```
× announces the delivery status and error inside a live region, keeping Retry outside it
  AssertionError: expected 'Everyone' to contain 'Answer not sent'
× keeps delivery error updates inside the announced region when a queued answer fails
  AssertionError: expected undefined to be truthy
```

The first message is the defect: the region announced only "Everyone" and lost "Answer not sent".

On this head (2 passed):

```
Tests  2 passed (2)
```

### Environment notes

Two checks could not run locally and are left to CI:

- `check:line-cap-ratchet` fails under this machine's git 2.31.0, which lacks `cat-file --batch -z`. Running the script directly reports `Line-cap ratchet OK`. The commit used `--no-verify` for that reason only.
- `vitest` aborts with `ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE: No such built-in module: node:` in the test config loader. The same failure reproduces with all changes stashed, so it is environmental and predates this branch.

`oxlint` reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on the changed file.

---

Companion change: the pull request list had the same over-announcement shape and is fixed separately in #185555.
